title: Neutrino Phone
one_liner: Compare light-speed latency through Earth's core versus around its surface between any two cities.
speaker: Alex Wisner-Gross
context: Wisner-Gross described wanting a neutrino-based communication link that shoots straight through the Earth, beating fiber or satellite paths that must follow the surface or orbit.
demo: Visitor picks two cities from a preset list (NYC-London, Tokyo-NY, Sydney-London, etc.) or drops pins on a simple world map. The tool computes the great-circle surface distance (today's fiber/satellite path) versus the straight chord through the Earth, converts both to light-speed latency, and animates two beams racing — one curving over the globe, one punching straight through — showing the millisecond savings, with a clear label that this is a speculative physics concept from the episode, not deployed technology.
data_plan: User input (city pairs) + bundled lat/long coordinates for ~20 major cities + basic geometry (great-circle vs chord distance) and speed of light constant, computed client-side.
risks: Must clearly label as a speculative thought experiment (neutrino detection/transmission at this scale doesn't exist); shouldn't imply the latency savings are achievable today.
